thread:
Anya (PM): Quick design check — ran a screenreader pass and a couple of keyboard-only flows on the routing policies editor preview. Found a mix of small copy nits and an accessibility surprise when reordering rules.
Sam (Design): ok noted. which reorder behavior felt off?
Anya (PM): When you keyboard-drag a rule its visual focus moves (good) but VoiceOver reads only 'button' repeatedly, not which rule moved or its new position. No aria-live announcement for order change.
Leo (Accessibility): yeah that's expected — we don't have an aria-live region on the stack reorder. We should announce "Rule X moved to position Y". Minimal, concise.
Miguel (Eng): adding a live region is doable. question: should it announce by rule name or by rule index? names can be long.
Sam (Design): prefer "<rule-label> moved to position <n>" — keeps it human, helps users confirm which one. If label is super long, collapse to prefix + ellipsis.
Kate (QA): also repro with screenreader + keyboard: after a move, focus sometimes lands on the placeholder handle instead of the moved item. Users lose context.
Miguel (Eng): hmm — I suspect the DOM reorder + focus management timing race is the cause. I can delay focus until the reorder animation completes or set focus explicitly after DOM update. Which is better?
Sam (Design): explicit focus to the moved item is best. animation is nice but we should not rely on timing.
Anya (PM): another UX copy thing: validation messages on rules panel read like errors from 2007. Eg: "Rule invalid: missing condition" — feels terse and unfriendly. Suggestion: "Add at least one condition so this rule can match traffic."
Sam (Design): yes — make them actionable. Also add subtle hint text under empty-state: "No rules yet — create a rule to route traffic." Current empty-state copy is just "No rules" which is ambiguous.
Leo (Accessibility): for empty states, include role="status" so assistive tech announces changes when a rule is added/removed.
Miguel (Eng): noted. I'll add role=status announcements for add/remove and implement aria-live for reorder.
Kate (QA): one more: preview simulation slider defaulting at 100% is confusing — designers expected it to show 10% to mimic canary traffic. Can we change the default to 10% when creating a new rollout?
Sam (Design): +1. Also update tooltip: "Simulation default mirrors a small canary — adjust to test different split ratios."
Anya (PM): yay. small thing on keyboard affordances: the drag handle is very narrow — keyboard focus ring only hits a few pixels. Can we widen the target or add a secondary 'move' control with explicit keyboard actions?
Sam (Design): adding a dedicated "Move" button is heavier. Maybe expand the hit area and expose up/down arrow keyboard ops when the handle is focused (aria-keyshortcuts: ArrowUp/ArrowDown).
Miguel (Eng): implementing arrow-based moves is straightforward. We'll need to ensure undo and aria announcements too.
deploy-bot: preview updated for branch feature/route-editor-a11y at 2147521200
Anya (PM): sweet — folks, action list?
Sam (Design): 1) update validation copy to be actionable (I'll draft). 2) widen hit area + add arrow-key moves (design + eng).
Miguel (Eng): 1) add aria-live reorder announcement "{label} moved to {pos}" 2) ensure focus lands on moved item 3) add role=status for empty state and add/remove events.
Leo (Accessibility): I'll run another VO + NVDA pass on the updated preview when ready.
Kate (QA): I'll add regression tests for keyboard reorder, focus, and preview slider default.
Anya (PM): timeline: Miguel and Sam — can we get a PR by end of week? Leo/Kate will test next Tues.
Miguel (Eng): yes, aiming for PR by Friday EOD.
Sam (Design): I'll drop copy edits in the doc and ping here when done. :thumbsup:
Anya (PM): thanks all — small nudges but big UX wins.
